Purpose

It was generated by scanning source files for class and function definitions and collecting the most relevant members. Use this as a working reference when planning refactors, tests or documentation work.

Summary

## 1) Core data models

File: `Momentum/Python/database/models.py`
- Classes:
  - `Driver`
    - Attributes: id, name, nationality, birth_date, age, 50+ skill attributes (raw_speed, consistency, racecraft, ...), career stats (career_wins, career_podiums...), biography, current_team_id, created_at, etc.
    - Methods / properties:
      - `get_discipline_rating(discipline: str) -> float` — computes rating for a discipline
      - `get_overall_rating() -> float`
      - `skill` (property alias for raw_speed) (*)
      - `adaptability` (property) (*)
      - `aggression` (property) (*)
      - `first_name`, `last_name` (*)

  - `Team`
    - Attributes: id, name, nationality, founded_year, discipline, tier, budget, headquarters, team_principal, biography, totals, financial & AI traits (financial_stability, management_quality, innovation_focus, risk_appetite...)
    - No complex methods defined in this dataclass (behaviour is primarily data holder)

  - `Track` (Track/Circuit model)
    - Attributes: id, name, country, region, circuit_type, ima_grade, primary_discipline, geometry (length_km, turns, left_turns, right_turns...), environmental factors, facilities, legacy fields, created_at

  - `Championship`
    - Attributes: id, name, discipline, tier, season_length, points_system (JSON), current_season, founded_year

  - `Race`
    - Attributes: id, championship_id, track_id, season, round_number, race_date, weather_conditions, race_duration_minutes, status
    - Properties: `circuit_id()` (alias), `discipline()` (alias/placeholder)

  - `RaceResult`
    - Attributes: id, race_id, driver_id, team_id, position, points, fastest_lap (bool), dnf_reason, grid_position

Notes: the module defines `SCHEMA_SQL` with full CREATE TABLE DDL used to create or verify the schema.

Related: `Momentum/Python/database/models/*.py` contains multi-discipline and staff/supplier model partitions (see below).

## 3) Discipline engines & simulation

File: `Momentum/Python/disciplines/base_engine.py`
- Classes:
  - `RacingDiscipline` (Enum)
  - `RaceEventType` (Enum)
  - `DisciplineContext` (dataclass) — bundles race, track, drivers, teams, weather
  - `BaseDisciplineEngine(ABC)` — abstract base for all discipline engines
    - Abstract methods expected by subclasses: e.g., `simulate_race(context)`, `calculate_performance(...)` (see file for exact abstract methods)

File: `Momentum/Python/disciplines/race_simulation.py`
- Classes:
  - `SimulationContext` — runtime context for a simulation
  - `RaceSimulator` — high-level Monte-Carlo style simulation driver
    - Responsibilities: orchestrate monte-carlo runs, combine environmental and driver/team weights

File: `Momentum/Python/disciplines/*_engine.py` (per-discipline)
- Example classes (subclassing BaseDisciplineEngine):
  - `SingleSeaterEngine` (single_seater/single_seater_engine.py)
  - `EnduranceEngine` (endurance/endurance_engine.py)
  - `RallyStageEngine` (rally_stage/rally_stage_engine.py)
  - `SprintRallycrossEngine` (sprint_rallycross/sprint_rallycross_engine.py)
  - `UrbanStreetEngine` (urban_street/urban_street_engine.py)
  - `DragAccelerationEngine` (drag_acceleration/drag_acceleration_engine.py)
  - `ProductionTouringEngine` (production_touring/production_touring_engine.py)

Each engine defines discipline-specific weighting, rulebook references and helper methods (for e.g., stage processing, joker lap handling, pit stop windows). For planning, note:
- Each discipline exposes `simulate`/`run_event` style methods and imports `BaseDisciplineEngine` requirements.
- Discipline config and rulebook modules provide constants and validation methods.

## 4) Systems (game systems and management)

Directory: `Momentum/Python/systems/`
- This contains the bulk of gameplay systems: championship_manager, game_loop, standings_manager, staff_management, vehicle_development, component_manager, component_integration, race_weekend, world_state, realistic_team_generator, realistic_circuit_generator, comprehensive_circuit_generator, etc.

Representative classes and methods (planning-focused summary):

- `ChampionshipManager` (`systems/championship_manager.py`)
  - Manages season calendars, driver contracts, transfer markets (`DriverContract`, `SeasonCalendar`, `TransferMarket` inner classes exist)
  - Methods: initialisation, schedule generation, contract resolution, transfer windows, season tick actions

- `GameLoop` (`systems/game_loop.py`)
  - Primary game loop orchestration; tracks season state, championship standings, event sequencing
  - Key methods: scheduling and rollover, run_tick / advance_time / process_event

- `StandingsManager` (`systems/standings_manager.py`)
  - Maintains `DriverStanding`, `ConstructorStanding`, `ChampionshipStandings`
  - Methods: `initialize_championship()`, `update_with_race_results()`, `add_qualifying_results()`, `get_standings()`, `get_driver_position()`, `_update_positions()`

- `ComponentManager` & `ComponentIntegration` (`systems/component_manager.py`, `systems/component_integration.py`)
  - Manage vehicle components, damage/wear, conversion between canonical `Vehicle` objects and runtime `RaceCar` objects
  - Notable methods in `ComponentIntegration`: `create_race_car_from_vehicle()`, `update_vehicle_from_race_car()`, `simulate_race_session()`, `handle_crash()`, `perform_pit_stop()`, `get_component_health_ui()`, `save_component_states()` and `load_component_states()`

- `VehicleDevelopmentEngine` / `VehicleCreationHelper` (`systems/vehicle_development.py`, `systems/vehicle_creation_helper.py`)
  - Methods for calculating development cost/time, simulate component interaction, calculate_overall_performance

- `StaffManagementSystem` (`systems/staff_management.py`)
  - Manages staff market, hiring/firing, and staff performance effects. Methods to evaluate candidates, apply worker effects and market simulation.

- Generators (team/circuit): `RealisticTeamGenerator`, `ComprehensiveCircuitGenerator`, `RealisticCircuitGenerator`
  - Methods to generate data, export to JSON, and deterministic seeding.

Planning notes:
- Systems modules contain many interdependencies; prioritize writing integration tests around `ComponentIntegration`, `RaceWeekendManager`, `GameLoop` and `StandingsManager` for core gameplay correctness.

## Expanded inventory: helpers, small classes, enums and utility functions (planning focus)

This section increases the breadth of the inventory to include many helper classes, enums, small data containers and utility functions that are used across the codebase and are important to the planned feature set.

Note: the list below is organised by subsystem and highlights small helpers (enums, config dataclasses, inner classes, small adapters) that are often overlooked but are critical for integration and test planning.

### A) Database / models helpers
- `Momentum/Python/database/models.py` and partitioned model modules:
  - Enums: discipline tuples and mapping constants (used to validate `discipline` fields in CREATE TABLE)
  - `SCHEMA_SQL` (string) — canonical CREATE TABLE DDL used in tests and database creation scripts
  - Helpers (in other model modules): currency, mock currency systems used in staff model tests

### B) Small helper dataclasses and adapters
- `Momentum/Python/disciplines/race_simulation.py`
  - `SimulationContext` — bundles inputs needed by `RaceSimulator` and discipline engines; used extensively for test harnesses
  - Small utility functions to normalise driver/team weights

- `Momentum/Python/systems/standings_manager.py`
  - `DriverStanding`, `ConstructorStanding`, `ChampionshipStandings` — small value objects used by UI and persistence

- `Momentum/Python/systems/race_weekend.py`
  - `SessionResult`, `RaceWeekendResults` — small containers used by `RaceWeekendManager` to accumulate qualifiers, sprint results, main race

### C) Enums & config objects (cross-cutting)
- Many modules expose Enums: `RacingDiscipline`, `RaceEventType`, `CircuitType`, `SurfaceType`, `Climate`, `EnduranceRaceLength`, `RacePhase`, `DecisionType`, etc. These are vital for validating inputs and for deterministic rule selection in discipline engines.

### D) Component & vehicle helpers
- `Momentum/Python/vehicles/components/*` often include:
  - small value classes (e.g., `Tire`), factories for component sets, and `__post_init__` normalisers in dataclasses
  - helper functions to compute combined metrics (power-to-weight, effective_downforce, braking_efficiency)

### E) Persistence & IO utilities
- `Momentum/Python/systems/component_persistence.py` — serialisation helpers to save/load component states used by save files and by build scripts
- `Momentum/Python/scripts/*` provide CLI-style helper wrappers that call into these persistence methods; they also demonstrate intended usage patterns for those utilities

### F) Testing utilities
- `Momentum/Python/tests/examples/driver_examples.py` and other test helper modules define factory functions / fixtures used across the test suite (create_demo_driver(), create_demo_team(), seeded_random())

## Use-case mapping: classes/helpers ranked by priority

Below I map the project's high-level use cases (as inferred from the report and code) to the classes and helpers that implement them. Each mapping includes a suggested priority (High/Medium/Low) from the perspective of delivering a playable, testable system.

Legend: Priority — High (core gameplay path), Medium (important support systems), Low (nice-to-have / polish)

Use case: Quick Race (user starts a single race with minimal setup)
- Priority: High
- Key classes/helpers:
  - `SimulationService` (`services/simulation_service.py`) — API wrapper to run races
  - `RaceSimulator` (`disciplines/race_simulation.py`) — monte-carlo engine
  - Discipline engine for chosen discipline (e.g., `SingleSeaterEngine`)
  - `ComponentIntegration.create_race_car_from_vehicle()` — prepare runtime `RaceCar` object
  - `RaceWeekendManager` / `Race` dataclass — orchestrates sessions
  - Test hooks: `tests/quick_test_race.py`
- Suggested acceptance tests: end-to-end quick race completes within U-R6 latency bound; result payload validates against schema

Use case: Full Season Simulation (initialize season, run all rounds, compute standings)
- Priority: High
- Key classes/helpers:
  - `GameLoop` (`systems/game_loop.py`) — season orchestration
  - `ChampionshipManager` (`systems/championship_manager.py`) — schedule + contracts
  - `StandingsManager` (`systems/standings_manager.py`) — ranking and points
  - `RaceSimulator` and discipline engines
  - DB persistence via `DatabaseManager`
- Suggested acceptance tests: run sample season script (`tests/test_2025_season.py`), validate standings and invariants (total points distribution)

Use case: Team Management (hire/fire staff, develop car, manage budget)
- Priority: High → Medium (core for management gameplay)
- Key classes/helpers:
  - `StaffManagementSystem` (`systems/staff_management.py`) — hiring/firing and staff market
  - `VehicleDevelopmentEngine` / `CarDevelopmentManager` (`systems/vehicle_development.py`, `car_development.py`)
  - `TeamManager` (`systems/team_management.py`) — budgets, finances and contract enforcement
  - `DatabaseManager` — persist staff/contract changes
- Suggested acceptance tests: contract lifecycle tests, staff effect on vehicle performance (unit + integration)

Use case: Garage / Components (inspect, repair, upgrade components)
- Priority: Medium
- Key classes/helpers:
  - `ComponentManager` and `ComponentIntegration` — health, service and persistent state
  - Components (`vehicles/components/*`) — service/rebuild APIs
  - `ComponentPersistence` — save/load states
- Suggested acceptance tests: component wear simulation, service reduces wear; persistence roundtrip

Use case: Emergent Narrative & Highlights (generate human-readable highlights)
- Priority: Medium → Low
- Key classes/helpers:
  - `RaceSimulator` summarisation routines
  - `SimulationService` + UI feed connectors
  - Small helpers that format highlight text
- Suggested acceptance tests: a sample race yields at least one highlight; highlight format meets spec

Use case: REST API & External Integration (documented endpoints)
- Priority: High
- Key classes/helpers:
  - `simulation.py` FastAPI endpoints
  - `api/schemas.py` — Pydantic models and contract
  - `SimulationService`
- Suggested acceptance tests: contract tests, latency/performance tests for core endpoints (U-R1/U-R9)

Use case: Save/Load and Export
- Priority: Medium
- Key classes/helpers:
  - `ComponentPersistence`, `DatabaseManager` exports, `scripts/*` for dump/import
  - `RaceResult`/export JSON support in services
- Suggested acceptance tests: export of ≤10k rows within U-R15-1 limits; exported JSON validates against schema

## Gaps identified (priority mapping + recommended fixes)

- Gap: limited explicit facades for high-coupling modules — `GameLoop`, `ComponentIntegration` and `DatabaseManager` are large and used directly by many callers.
  - Risk: refactors will produce many breakages across systems.
  - Recommendation: introduce small, well-tested facades for these subsystems that provide a narrow, versioned interface for other modules and GUI.

- Gap: missing contract tests for API endpoints and schema evolution tracking.
  - Recommendation: add `tests/api_contract_tests.py` that uses `api/schemas.py` to validate runtime responses.

- Gap: test harness standardisation — some tests are standalone scripts rather than pytest-style tests.
  - Recommendation: pick a primary test runner (pytest) and convert scripts that are intended as automated tests.
